Which country, after Norway, had the highest share of electric cars in new car sales last year? Nepal, at 68%.

I opened with that question at today’s SDG7 Action Forum in New York. We often describe SDG7 through its gaps: 655 million people without electricity and two billion without clean cooking. But that account misses how quickly energy markets are changing.

Solar’s share of global electricity has risen from 1% to around 9% in a decade. Developing and emerging economies will account for 85% of electricity demand growth through 2035. Three priorities follow:

Build the systems around the power. Africa is heading for around 17 GW of new solar this year. Grids and storage must keep pace. In Mauritius, UNDP has supported smart-grid technology and 18 MW of battery storage.

Lower financing costs. The same solar project can face two to three times the cost of capital in many emerging economies. A one percentage point reduction could save US$150 billion a year.

Keep more value locally. Electricity should power farms, businesses, and industry. Yet of 16.6 million renewable energy jobs worldwide, only 344,000 are in Africa.

By 2030, how much of the transition’s value will stay in the countries producing its power?
